entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. The variant that milasen targets is a gained cryptic splice acceptor 119 bp upstream of a retrotransposon insertion deep in an intron, with exon 6 missplicing into it; this is a gain-of-site mechanism, with the canonical sites not described as destroyed.
entries.snippet: revealed missplicing of exon 6 into a cryptic splice-acceptor site (i6.SA) in MFSD8 intron 6, in a location 119 bp upstream from the SVA insertion site

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. The oligonucleotides were designed to target the cryptic acceptor and nearby enhancers, i.e. to mask a harmful site, and the lead candidate raised normal to mutant splicing ratios in patient fibroblasts.
entries.snippet: we designed antisense oligonucleotides to target the i6.SA cryptic splice-acceptor site and nearby splice enhancers (Fig. 2A)
entries.anchor: Results, Development of an Antisense Oligonucleotide Drug

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. In patient fibroblasts the lead drug more than tripled normal exon 6 to exon 7 splicing by RNA-seq, a relative increase in normal splicing, not complete correction.
entries.snippet: RNA-seq from patient fibroblasts showed that milasen treatment more than tripled the amount of normal (exon 6–exon 7) splicing (Fig. 2C).
